questions.answer: Mostly in Sirajganj, although I spent many school holidays at my grandparents' home in our village nearby. Both places shaped me, and I still feel a strong sense of [[belonging]] whenever I go back.

questions.q: What did you enjoy doing as a child?
questions.answer: I was quite an outdoorsy kid. I'd spend hours playing cricket with the neighbourhood children until it got dark. Looking back, those were some of the most [[carefree]] times of my life.

questions.q: Did you have any hobbies as a child?
questions.answer: Plenty. I was always outside playing cricket, and I also loved reading comics and adventure stories. Those simple hobbies kept me endlessly [[entertained]], long before phones and screens took over.

questions.q: Did you have much freedom as a child?
questions.answer: Quite a lot, compared to children in big cities today. As long as I was home before dark, my parents were fairly relaxed. Our neighbourhood felt safe, so I could [[roam]] around with friends quite freely.

questions.q: Do you think children today have a better childhood than you had?
questions.answer: In some ways, yes. They have access to far more information and opportunities. However, I think they spend too much time indoors on screens and miss out on the kind of [[unstructured]] outdoor play I enjoyed.
